report.source_text: Three weeks later, the patient showed subjective and objective improvement in ocular symptoms. Visual acuity improved to 20/20 bilaterally, with normal IOP. Slit lamp examination revealed clear and unremarkable anterior segments bilaterally. Mild lower vitritis (0.5 + cells) was found in both eyes. Fundus examination revealed mild elevation and slight blurring of the nasal optic disc bilaterally. In the right eye, the macula appeared dry with two small, pinpoint, paracentral well-defined hypopigmented foci and no signs of inflammation in the peripheral retina. In the left eye, a dry macula with a small hypopigmented focus was located nasally to the fovea, and there was no inflammation on the periphery.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old male soldier presented with a 7-day history of right eye paracentral scotoma and 2-day history of dark spots in the left eye, preceded by systemic symptoms including two weeks of 39°C fever, headache, night sweats, transient rash, and 10 kg weight loss. Initial labs showed thrombocytosis, elevated atypical lymphocytes, elevated liver enzymes, and ESR of 24 mm/hr. Infectious workup was negative for toxoplasmosis and syphilis but positive for Rickettsia typhi serology. Ophthalmic examination revealed bilateral mild optic disc elevation and blurriness with small yellowish retinitis foci adjacent to the fovea in both eyes. Fluorescein angiography showed bilateral mild optic disc hyperfluorescence without vascular leakage; indocyanine green angiography demonstrated small hypofluorescent foci in the left macula and nasal to the disc. Abdominal ultrasound was normal despite liver enzyme elevation. The patient was treated with doxycycline and prednisone, leading to subjective and objective improvement at 3 weeks with resolution of ocular inflammation and recovery of visual acuity to 20/20 bilaterally.
